summary: Guaifenesin is an over-the-counter expectorant used for the symptomatic relief of productive (chesty) cough. It loosens phlegm (mucus) and thins bronchial secretions to help clear the airways and make coughs more productive. It is available as immediate-release and extended-release (bi-layer) tablets, with a maximum adult dose of 2400 mg per day. It is generally well tolerated; cough that persists beyond 7 days, recurs, or is accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache should prompt medical evaluation as it may signal a more serious illness.
indications: Helps loosen phlegm (mucus) and thin bronchial secretions to rid the bronchial passageways of bothersome mucus and make coughs more productive

moa: Guaifenesin acts as an expectorant by increasing the output and reducing the viscosity of respiratory tract fluid. By stimulating respiratory secretions, it thins and loosens bronchial mucus, promoting ciliary clearance and making coughs more productive so that bothersome phlegm can be cleared from the airways.

relative: Persistent or chronic cough such as occurs with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema (ask a doctor before use)
Cough accompanied by excessive phlegm (mucus) (ask a doctor before use)
monitor: Development of fever, rash, or persistent headache

preg: If pregnant, ask a health professional before use. The OTC label does not establish safety in pregnancy and advises consulting a healthcare professional before using the product.
lact: If breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use. The OTC label advises consulting a healthcare professional before using the product while breast-feeding.
renal: The OTC label does not specify a renal dose adjustment. Use the lowest effective dose and consult a healthcare professional in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: The OTC label does not specify a hepatic dose adjustment. Consult a healthcare professional in significant hepatic impairment.

interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals; take with a full glass of water.
interactions.alcohol: No specific alcohol interaction is stated on the OTC label.
interactions.diagnostics: Guaifenesin metabolites may interfere with certain urinary catecholamine and 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) laboratory determinations; the OTC label does not list specific interferences.

emergency: Signs of a serious underlying illness if cough is accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache

pearls: Designed for productive (chesty) cough - loosens mucus rather than suppressing the cough reflex
Extended-release bi-layer 600 mg tablets are dosed every 12 hours; do not crush or chew
Maximum adult dose is 2400 mg in 24 hours
Adequate fluid intake supports the expectorant effect
A cough lasting more than 7 days or recurring with fever/rash/persistent headache warrants medical evaluation
missed: As an as-needed cough remedy, take a dose when needed; if you forget a scheduled dose, take it when you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, then skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once and do not exceed the maximum daily amount.
overdose: In case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away. Overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, and gastrointestinal upset; management is supportive.
